jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in North Carolina, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in North Carolina, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, NC Senate, NC House and U.S. House districts, townships, municipalities, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: North Carolina district map, what district am I in, NC Senate district, NC House district, county commissioner district, North Carolina township, NC school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in North Carolina, and who represents you there.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 14 congressional districts — the largest districts North Carolina carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 14 features for North Carolina, measured 2026-10-09. These are the districts the current members were elected from; the 120th Congress's map, redrawn in 2025, takes over when they leave office on 3 January 2027.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: NC Senate District
layers.rank_note: 50 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The North Carolina Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 50 features, measured 2026-09-29. Simplified in ONE mapshaper run with both other chambers, because a shared edge only survives identically off one topology.

source.people: nc-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Open States current-people export for North Carolina (name, party, e-mail, links). What the General Assembly publishes beyond that is recorded in nc/WATCH.md rather than assumed.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 100 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, who won each seat on its board of commissioners, and who sits on the board of the soil and water conservation district that covers it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 100 features, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: Every county's board of commissioners, each seat named for the winner of its most recent election in the North Carolina State Board of Elections' results (the 2022 and 2024 generals), read with the State Board's candidate filing lists for each seat's term and dated to that election; rebuilt weekly by nc/scripts/build_nc_county_commissioners.py. A winner is not a sitting member: a board fills a vacancy by appointment, which no result records, and the card says so. A seat the 2026 filing list shows has changed hands names nobody and says why. Three limited-voting counties' seat counts were read from the counties' own board pages; Tyrrell's could not be, so its board names nobody. Every seat in the county is listed because no publisher draws commissioner districts (G.S. 153A-22(f) keeps them as written descriptions in each clerk's office). The card also names the supervisors of the county's soil and water conservation district, from the Division of Soil and Water Conservation's District Directory, one PDF printed from the division's database, read by nc/scripts/build_nc_conservation_boards.py: each supervisor's office on the board, whether the seat is elected or appointed, and the term; re-read quarterly and after each November election (nc/WATCH.md). A seat the directory lists with no name is shown that way and never as a vacancy, and the Albemarle district's supervisors are listed county by county, as the directory lists them.

layers.label: NC House District
layers.rank_note: 120 House districts — the smallest of the three chamber tilings

source.answers: The North Carolina House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 120 features, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: nc-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Open States current-people export for North Carolina.

layers.label: Superior Court District
layers.rank_note: 73 superior court districts, 1,909 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-20 on the drawn file — smaller on average than a State Senate district (2,788 km2), larger than a county (1,394)

source.answers: The superior court district covering the point: its division, its counties and the parts of the counties the law divides, how many resident superior court judges the law gives it and whether any seat is tied to a county, the districts that share a senior resident judge, and, for the two districts the law ends on 1 January 2029, that date.

boundary.label: North Carolina General Statutes — G.S. 7A-41 as the General Assembly publishes it, read 2026-10-20 and kept in nc/data/source/statutes/: subsection (a) lists each district's counties and judges, and subsection (b) the 2010 Census voting districts and blocks of each part of the nine counties it divides. Drawn on the shipped county file by nc/scripts/build_nc_court_districts.py and shipped with the app.
U.S. Census TIGERweb — Census 2010, voting districts (layer 72) and blocks (layer 18): the 2010 lines G.S. 7A-41(c) and (c1) say govern, read 2026-10-20 for the nine divided counties.
G.S. 7A-41.1 — districts that together make up the same counties share one senior resident superior court judge

source.people: NO JUDGE IS NAMED. The court system lists who serves in its judicial directory, and www.nccourts.gov's robots.txt disallows that page for every client (measured 2026-10-20), so the card links it instead; election results cannot stand in for it, because the Governor fills a seat that comes open between elections. Recorded as gap nc-judges. The card gives the number of judges the law sets for the district and, for District 31A, where G.S. 7A-41(a) and (b) give different numbers, gives both and states neither.
source.applies: North Carolina — statewide, all 73 districts (71 from 1 January 2029, when the law ends Districts 10E and 31D).

layers.label: District Court District
layers.rank_note: 47 district court districts, 2,966 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-20 on the drawn file — larger on average than a State Senate district (2,788 km2), smaller than a congressional district (9,956)

source.answers: The district court district covering the point: its counties and the parts of the two counties the law divides, how many district judges the law gives it, and whether any seat is tied to a county.

boundary.label: North Carolina General Statutes — G.S. 7A-133 as the General Assembly publishes it, read 2026-10-20 and kept in nc/data/source/statutes/: subsection (a) lists each district's counties and judges, and subsection (b) the 2010 Census voting districts of the districts inside Wake and Vance Counties. Drawn on the shipped county file by nc/scripts/build_nc_court_districts.py and shipped with the app.
U.S. Census TIGERweb — Census 2010, voting districts (layer 72): the 2010 lines G.S. 7A-133(b) says govern, read 2026-10-20 for Wake and Vance Counties.
G.S. 7A-140 — each district judge is elected by the voters of the district, lives in it and serves four years

source.people: NO JUDGE IS NAMED. The court system lists who serves in its judicial directory, and www.nccourts.gov's robots.txt disallows that page for every client (measured 2026-10-20), so the card links it instead; election results cannot stand in for it, because the Governor fills a seat that comes open between elections. Recorded as gap nc-judges. The card gives the number of judges the law sets for the district and, for Districts 12 and 32, where G.S. 7A-133(a) and its residence paragraphs give different numbers, gives both and states neither.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 118 unified (K-12) districts covering the whole state, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 118 features for North Carolina, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. North Carolina's boards of education are elected, and no statewide roster of their members was found in this pass — recorded as a gap rather than left unstated.
source.applies: North Carolina — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary-only and secondary-only tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in North Carolina (0 features each, measured 2026-09-29), so one tiling ships where Illinois ships three.

layers.label: Township
layers.rank_note: 1,041 county subdivisions — North Carolina townships, the census fabric below the county

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 1,041 features for North Carolina, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A North Carolina township is a census and historical unit with no governing board of its own, unlike Illinois's, so the card is identity-only and says so. MEASURED CAVEAT: at least two counties (Gaston, Hyde) name their COMMISSIONER districts after townships in their certified returns, so a township can carry an electoral function even where it has no government — recorded in nc/WATCH.md rather than generalised from two counties.

layers.label: School Board District
layers.rank_note: 423 pieces on the boards of 38 school districts that elect members by district, pre-built from the State Board of Elections' precinct-level results — the 421 under Durham's two consolidated districts a mean 117.0 km2 (median 74.5), measured 2026-10-17 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a county subdivision (1,041 tiling the state's 139,389 km2, a mean 133.9), larger than a voting precinct (median 25.32)

source.answers: The election district of a North Carolina school board that elects members by district, and the school district whose board it is. Where one election's ballots in a precinct carried two of a board's districts, both are named; where different elections put different districts on the ballot, each election's are named and none is chosen; where the results place no current district seat, the card says so.

boundary.label: North Carolina State Board of Elections — precinct-level election results (results_pct_<date>.zip), one file for each election from May 17, 2022 to the November 3, 2026 ballot the State Board posted on October 5, 2026: each district is the precincts whose ballots carried its seat's latest contest, cut to the school district. Read 2026-10-17 and pre-built by nc/scripts/build_nc_school_board_districts.py, shipped with the app. The State Board's ShapeFiles folder carries its precinct maps and no map of these districts.

North Carolina State Board of Elections — its statewide precinct maps (SBE_PRECINCTS_<date>.zip), nine dated January 18, 2022 to August 24, 2026: each election's precincts are read in the map holding the most of that election's precinct codes, read 2026-10-17.
U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts): the boundary each board's districts are cut to, read 2026-10-17.

source.people: NO MEMBER IS NAMED YET. The results name each contest's winner, but a board fills a vacancy by appointment, which no results file records, and the seats on the November 3, 2026 ballot stay with the members serving now until that election's winners take office. Matching the winners to the members serving now has not been done, so the card names no one rather than guessing — recorded as gap nc-school-board-members. The card links each board's school district website instead: the address that the National Center for Education Statistics' Common Core of Data district directory for the 2025-26 school year gives, kept where it answered with a page when the file was built, which all 38 did on 2026-10-17.
source.applies: The 38 North Carolina school districts whose boards elect members by district, measured 2026-10-17 from the results as the boards whose district seats are each voted on in only part of the school district: Alexander, Anson, Beaufort, Bladen, Buncombe, Caswell, Charlotte-Mecklenburg, Craven, Cumberland, Duplin, Durham, Edenton-Chowan, Edgecombe, Forsyth, Franklin, Granville, Guilford, Harnett, Hickory City, Iredell-Statesville, Lenoir, Lexington City, Madison, Martin, Montgomery, Nash-Rocky Mount, Newton-Conover City, Pamlico, Pitt, Robeson, Rockingham, Union, Vance, Wake, Watauga, Wayne, Whiteville City and Wilson. 45 boards are elected at large, and 32 more label seats by district while every precinct votes on each of them; neither kind has districts to draw, and the empty card says so.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 853 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping North Carolina, of the 1,668 the Census counts in the state's own bounding box, in a mirrored tile archive (measured 2026-10-17)

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='37', and the envelope must be Esri's own {xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax} shape. 1,500 features in North Carolina's box, measured 2026-09-29 — and that round number was checked rather than trusted: the layer's maxRecordCount is 100,000 and splitting the box at longitude -80 returns 911 + 618, which is 1,500 plus the 29 ZCTAs the seam counts twice.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: North Carolina. A ZCTA is kept where it overlaps the state, so a click in Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia or South Carolina gets the layer's own empty note rather than a false silence or a neighbouring state's ZIP code.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 2,625 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the State Board of Elections' file as NC OneMap serves it — 53.10 km2 mean area, land and water (median 25.32), measured 2026-10-15 on the drawn file: smaller than the Qualla Boundary's pieces (median 107.2 km2), larger on average than a city or town (20.26 km2 of land)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: North Carolina State Board of Elections — the statewide precinct file (SBE_PRECINCTS_20260824), public information under G.S. 132-1, read from the queryable copy NC OneMap serves for the Center for Geographic Information and Analysis; 2,625 features, pre-built for the state by nc/scripts/build_nc_precincts.py and shipped with the app. The copy carries no date of its own; on 2026-10-15 it matched the Board's August 24, 2026 file in every county, which the card says.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 552 incorporated places, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 552 features for North Carolina, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: In the 42 cities and towns above 25,000 people, the mayor and every council member, alderman or commissioner, written down from each city's own pages and proved against those pages by nc/scripts/build_nc_city_councils.py, which fails when a name is no longer on the page it cites (nc/data/app/nc-city-councils.json). Where the page a seat cites prints an e-mail address or a telephone number beside that member alone, the card shows it, and the build proves it on that page in the same way; a line or mailbox the page gives the office or several members is not shown, and no street address is. Raleigh's and Matthews's names are the candidates with the most votes in the State Board of Elections' results, because both websites answer this app with a managed challenge, and the card says so. Each seat says whether its district's own voters or the whole city elect it, read from each city's own pages, because nothing the state publishes records it. North Carolina's other 510 cities, towns and villages name nobody yet, recorded as gap nc-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: North Carolina — statewide. A point outside every incorporated place is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: City Council District
layers.rank_note: 100 council districts and wards in the 17 cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by district or ward, ranked just after City or Town, which each one divides, so a district draws on top of its city

source.answers: The city council district or ward containing the point, in the 17 North Carolina cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by district or ward, and the member for it.

boundary.label: City of Charlotte — Council Districts, layer 0 of its CouncilDistricts service, which says it "shows the current city council district boundaries": 7 districts, read 2026-10-16, the district number alone requested. Its credit line names the city's Planning Department and states no licence.

City of Raleigh — Council Districts Scenario 2, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, published in November 2021 and described as "Proposed Council Districts, Scenario 2": 5 districts, read 2026-10-16. The city's live layer is closed to this project by its robots.txt, and the precincts that carried each district's contest on 5 November 2024 lie 99.9% to 100% inside the same district on this copy. It states no licence.
Guilford County — Greensboro Council Districts, layer 4 of its Elected_Representation service: 5 districts, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.
City of Winston-Salem — Wards, layer 0 of its Boundaries2 service: 8 wards, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.
City of Fayetteville — City Council Districts, layer 0 of its CityCouncilDistricts service: 9 districts, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.

Town of Cary — Town of Cary Council, layer 2 of its Elections service: 4 districts, read 2026-10-16, the district letter alone requested and the records with no district left out. Its service's credit line names the City of Naperville, Illinois, and Esri, and it states no licence.

Guilford County — High Point Council, layer 10 of its Elected_Representation service: 6 wards, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. Its credit line names Guilford County, and it states no licence.

City of Greenville — City Council Districts, layer 1 of its Published service: 5 districts, read 2026-10-16, the district number alone requested and a record whose district reads "Non Voting" left out. It states no licence.
City of Gastonia — Ward Number, layer 0 of its GastoniaCouncilWards service: 6 wards, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.

Onslow County — City of Jacksonville Wards, layer 60 of its TemplateSite OperationalLayers service: 4 wards, read 2026-10-16. The county also publishes a different map of the city's wards with its Census 2020 layers, which is not used. It states no licence.

City of Rocky Mount — City Council Districts, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, which says its boundaries "were voted on and finalized in 2022": 7 wards in 11 records, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. It states no licence.
Iredell County — Election Wards - Mooresville, layer 3 of its Elections service: 4 wards, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.

City of Wilson — Voting Districts, layer 34 of its communitymaps service: 7 districts, read 2026-10-16, the district number alone requested. Its credit line names City of Wilson GIS Services, and it states no licence.
City of Goldsboro — Elected Council Districts, layer 0 of its Election_Districts service: 6 districts, read 2026-10-16, a record numbered 0 that draws the whole city left out. It states no licence.

City of New Bern — New Bern Wards, layer 0 of its NewBern_Wards service: 6 wards in 11 records, read 2026-10-16, the ward number alone requested. Its credit line names the City of New Bern's GIS, and it states no licence.
Lee County — CouncilWards, layer 1 of its POLITICAL service: 5 wards in 58 records, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.
City of Statesville — Statesville Election Wards, in the city's ArcGIS Online organization, last edited 8 September 2026: 6 wards, read 2026-10-16. It states no licence.

source.people: The member for each district, from the same city council roster the City or Town card reads (nc/data/app/nc-city-councils.json), written down from each city's own pages (Raleigh's from the State Board of Elections' results) and proved against them by nc/scripts/build_nc_city_councils.py. Which seats a district elects was read from each city's own pages. Its check holds every drawn district to a seat its voters elect and every such seat to a drawn district. Gastonia's members for Wards 3, 4 and 6 were elected by the whole city, and the card says so.
source.applies: The 17 North Carolina cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by district or ward: Cary, Charlotte, Fayetteville, Gastonia, Goldsboro, Greensboro, Greenville, High Point, Jacksonville, Mooresville, New Bern, Raleigh, Rocky Mount, Sanford, Statesville, Wilson and Winston-Salem. Durham, Concord, Hickory and Morrisville tie seats to wards or districts and elect every one by the whole city, so a district there would elect no one of its own. Ground inside a city's Census outline that its map leaves out lies in no district here.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-09-29: 818 points in North Carolina's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: North Carolina — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in Virginia or South Carolina, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — North Carolina has 2 pieces, the Qualla Boundary's 211.753 km² and its 2.640 km² of trust land, both the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians', MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py; median 107.2 km². Drawn above ZIP codes and below cities and towns. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land by the state, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — North Carolina has 2 such areas, both the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians'.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: Nobody yet: the Eastern Band's site could not be read from where this project is built, and the card says so. The communities the Census draws on the land are named on the card. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Western North Carolina — the Qualla Boundary and its trust land. Most points in the state are on no tribal land.

anchor_point.note: the State Capitol block, downtown Raleigh, Wake County

negative_point.note: the open Atlantic east of Hatteras Island — outside every North Carolina county, measured 2026-09-29. IT HAS TO BE THE OCEAN: the TIGER county fabric is water-inclusive for the inland sounds, so Pamlico Sound is Hyde County and Albemarle Sound is Tyrrell, and a point picked off a map inside either would make this assertion vacuous. Inside permalink_gate's maxLng (-75.10) so the point is still selectable.

geometry.note: The whole-North-Carolina outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 100-county fabric.
The 100 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 14 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119) until 3 January 2027.
The 50 NC Senate districts. Simplified in the same mapshaper run as the other two chamber files.
The 120 NC House districts. Simplified in the same mapshaper run as the other two chamber files.

The 73 superior court districts G.S. 7A-41 writes, pre-built by nc/scripts/build_nc_court_districts.py from the kept statute text: whole counties from state-counties.json, and the nine divided counties from the 2010 Census voting districts and blocks the law lists (Douglas-Peucker at 5 m on each dividing line, and the build refuses a line that strays more than 8 m from the 2010 line it draws). 2.0 MB, 590 KB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The 47 district court districts G.S. 7A-133 writes, pre-built by the same builder: whole counties, and Wake's and Vance's districts from the 2010 Census voting districts the law lists. 1.57 MB, 470 KB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

North Carolina's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — the Qualla Boundary and its trust land, both the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians'. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-10-10; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Every North Carolina voting precinct, pre-built by nc/scripts/build_nc_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the State Board of Elections' file as NC OneMap serves it (Douglas-Peucker at 12 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.98% with zero overlaps; an exact 2,625 count on the fetch and the drawn file). 8.2 MB, 2.43 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The 100 council districts and wards of the 17 cities above 25,000 people that elect council members by district or ward, pre-built by nc/scripts/build_nc_city_wards.py through scripts/city_ward_maps.py from the map each city or its county publishes (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 6,800-point agreement gate over the seventeen cities' extents, measured 99.94%, with no overlap; each map held to its city's Census outline). 1.46 MB, 410 KB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The election districts of the 38 school boards that elect members by district, pre-built by nc/scripts/build_nc_school_board_districts.py from the State Board of Elections' precinct-level results and precinct maps, cut to the Census school districts (Douglas-Peucker at 15 m in one shared pass; an 8,443-point agreement gate, measured 99.657% with no point in two pieces; the widest hole between a board's pieces held under 90 m). 3.70 MB, 986 KB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on. The floor and ceiling are equal because the pieces follow the results: a new results file can move them, and that wants reading.

rosters.note: U.S. House (NC) roster, refreshed weekly by update-nc-congress-roster.yml.
NC Senate roster from Open States, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 50 because a vacant seat is a real event.
NC House roster from Open States, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 120 for the same reason.

Every county's board of commissioners, each seat the winner of its most recent general in the State Board of Elections' results, built by nc/scripts/build_nc_county_commissioners.py and refreshed weekly by update-nc-county-commissioners.yml.

The mayor and council of each of the 42 cities and towns above 25,000 people, keyed by Census place id, written down from each city's own pages and proved against them by nc/scripts/build_nc_city_councils.py, whose --check holds the file to its seats file, its record of every page read and the drawn districts. Every page it cites is re-read weekly (watch-city-council-pages.yml), which opens a tracking issue when a name or a contact has gone from its page and never edits the file; the seats file is changed by hand (nc/WATCH.md).
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.

The supervisors of the soil and water conservation district covering each county, keyed by county GEOID, read from the state's District Directory by nc/scripts/build_nc_conservation_boards.py, whose --check holds the file to its record of the directory read and to the County card's wording. Re-read quarterly and after each November election (nc/WATCH.md).
